items.title: Tiny Italian Wars
items.summary: The author paints tiny Podrek prints on one-inch bases for Battle-Axe, including Swiss pike blocks built from four strips per stand. The photos make it easy to compare how massed pike reads on a compact footprint.

items.title: Condottiere
items.summary: The author uses the 1440 Battle of Anghiari to narrow an interest in fifteenth-century Italian mercenary armies into a specific tabletop matchup. It’s a project lead for the generation before the Italian Wars.

imageRights.credit: The Battle of Anghiari, after Leonardo da Vinci, retouched by Peter Paul Rubens
imageRights.alt: Drawing of mounted soldiers fighting around a standard at Anghiari.

items.title: A Game of Galleys before the Wind
items.summary: Scratch-built galleys and a modified Crown and Skull ruleset put Venetian, Maltese, and allied squadrons up against the Ottomans. The report shows how the Maltese make early headway while other Ottoman squadrons close in.

items.title: Somewhere in Greece 1941
items.summary: A WWII Spearhead player turns Jeff Plowman’s histories into a plausible scenario for his 20mm collection. A mixed British force must fall back to a river line with Germans close behind.

items.title: Battle of Tapae, 101 AD, using Three Ages of Rome
items.summary: A Roman–Dacian refight with an order of battle adjusted to the collection and a quick-reference sheet adapted for 28mm play. The linked planning post covers the briefings, victory conditions, and design choices behind the game.

items.title: Spanish Civil War Crossfire in 20mm
items.summary: Two infantry companies fight across dense village terrain. The Republicans have to clear a position after the Nationalists gain ground early. The game shows how much Crossfire gets out of terrain, initiative, and machine guns.

items.title: “WW2-ish” Company Level Rules
items.summary: A rules-design discussion built around a company of infantry and a few supporting weapons or vehicles, with a stand per squad or attachment. The author explains what makes FiveCore Company Command easy to teach and which mechanics are worth carrying forward.

items.title: Operation Martlet — BIG Bolt Action
items.summary: A Normandy club game makes St Nicolas Farm the gateway to Rauray while German reserves gather. A house rule lets a single order die activate nearby units, keeping the large game moving with fewer dice in the bag.

items.title: A German Reconnaissance Mission
items.summary: A solo desert scenario asks a reconnaissance force to find out what is defending a farm complex. Colored markers represent possible Commonwealth contacts of different weights, an idea you could borrow for hidden defenders on a small table.

items.title: Bloody Big Battles, Gettysburg
items.summary: A 15mm practice game with photos of Buford’s delaying action, Union reinforcements, and the ground around the Round Tops. See how the game marks arrival times and makes a multi-day battle readable.

items.title: Raseiniai, 24 June 1941 — Again
items.summary: The players swap sides for a second run of the scenario. The German player uses lessons from the first game to defend four objectives, while the Soviet player concentrates on a central hamlet.

items.title: Soldiers of Napoleon: French Imperial Guard vs 1814 Austrians
items.summary: French Guard infantry and heavy cavalry face an Austrian line anchored on a bog and a small copse. The players field 10mm French and 15mm Austrians together, worth a look if mixed collections are keeping a matchup off the table.

items.title: Rediscovering DBR
items.summary: A short report on bringing 15mm Royalists and Parliamentarians back out to relearn De Bellis Renationis. The photos and brief account make it an easy look at an established pike-and-shot ruleset.

items.title: Maurikian Byzantine versus Arab Conquest
items.summary: Arab light camelry threaten the Byzantine rear while cultivated fields disrupt another advance. The photos make the interaction between flank movement and difficult ground easy to follow.

items.title: The Ottomans Are Coming!
items.summary: A fictional Pike & Shotte scenario pits the Ottomans against Muscovite, Polish, and Cossack forces around a fortified town. Cavalry on both wings outruns the advancing infantry, giving several parts of the table distinct jobs.

items.title: Battle of San Francisco, South America, 1879
items.summary: A photographed 15mm Volley and Bayonet refight set in Peru during the War of the Pacific. It shows what an established mass-battle ruleset can do with a period that seldom shows up in the usual feed.

items.title: Gaming — Trafalgar
items.summary: Every ship is represented in this refight using Rod Langton’s detailed rules. The group uses revised play sheets to streamline handling, addressing the practical problem of making a large naval game run at the table.

imageRights.credit: Photo by Dave Docherty, One Man and His Brushes
imageRights.alt: Rows of miniature sailing ships deployed across the Trafalgar gaming table.

items.title: Pony Wars Buildings — 6mm
items.summary: A short photo post on finishing a Pendraken house, frontier farm, and barn over a weekend. Useful visual reference for how much detail is worth picking out on tiny buildings.

items.title: Painting an Army for a King (of Kings)
items.summary: A 10mm Persian project for To the Strongest! reaches the point where the infantry is done. The Greek mercenary hoplite stands match earlier bases so they can also work in a separate Greek army.

items.title: Xyston Thracian Archers
items.summary: Work-in-progress photos show what basing contributes at small scale. The author builds the ground from wood filler and railway ballast, then adds a drybrush, static grass, and tufts.

items.title: 10mm Early Medieval Commission: Viking and Norman Generals and Skirmishers
items.summary: Front, side, and overhead views show command groups and skirmishers, including crossbowmen. A quick reference for making leaders readable in a 1066 collection.

items.title: Terrain — More Russian-style Buildings
items.summary: The author paints printed buildings over a dark undercoat with staggered earth-tone drybrushes and picked-out windows and doors. A straightforward batch approach for making a village read well at gaming distance.

imageRights.credit: Photo by Dave Docherty, One Man and His Brushes
imageRights.alt: Painted wooden buildings, mounted miniatures, and tracks on a model railway embankment.

items.title: 10mm Pendraken Hedges and Modern Street Furniture
items.summary: Multi-tone hedges, skips, phone boxes, and plinths get finished in a spare afternoon. The photo set shows how to add recognizable detail without taking up much room on a small board.

items.title: Japanese Support — Sino-Japanese War
items.summary: A look at finishing Japanese support teams for a project outside the usual European WWII rotation. It includes figures from two makers and a note on the work still needed to translate one of the teams into game stats.

items.title: The Other Partizan 2026 Walkthrough
items.summary: A vertical video takes you through the participation and demonstration areas at Newark in under half an hour. It’s a way to discover clubs, table ideas, and periods in one phone-friendly video.
